title: Legislative districts of Davao del Sur
wikitext:
{{Short description|None}} {{Politics of the Philippines}} The '''legislative districts of Davao del Sur''' are the representations of the [[Provinces of the Philippines|province]] of [[Davao del Sur]] in the [[List of legislatures of the Philippines|various national legislatures]] of the [[Philippines]]. The province is currently represented in the [[House of Representatives of the Philippines|lower house]] of the [[Congress of the Philippines]] through its [[#Lone District|lone congressional district]]. [[Davao City]] and [[Davao Occidental]] last formed part of the province's representation in 1972 and 2016, respectively. == History == {{further|Legislative district of Mindanao and Sulu|Legislative district of Davao}} Prior to gaining separate representation, areas now under the jurisdiction of Davao del Sur were represented under the [[Department of Mindanao and Sulu]] (1917–1935) and the historical [[Davao (province)|Davao Province]] (1935–1967). The enactment of Republic Act No. 4867 on May 8, 1967 split the old Davao Province into [[Davao del Norte]], [[Davao del Sur]] and [[Davao Oriental]].{{cite web|title=Republic Act No. 4867 - An Act Creating the Provinces of Davao del Norte, Davao del Sur and Davao Oriental|date=May 8, 1967|access-date=February 3, 2017|author=Congress of the Philippines|website=Chan Robles Virtual Law Library|url=http://laws.chanrobles.com/republicacts/49_republicacts.php?id=4871}} Per Section 4 of R.A. 4867, the incumbent Davao Province representative was to indicate which of the three new provinces he wished to continue to represent; Rep. Lorenzo Sarmiento chose [[Legislative districts of Davao del Norte#Lone District (defunct)|Davao del Norte]], which left the seats for [[#1968–1972|Davao del Sur]] (together grouped with the chartered city of [[Davao City|Davao]]) and [[Legislative districts of Davao Oriental#Lone District (defunct)|Davao Oriental]] open for the [[List of special elections to the Philippine Congress#House of Representatives|special elections]] scheduled for November 14, 1967. [[Davao del Sur]], along with [[Davao City]], were [[#1968–1972|represented together]] from the second half of the [[6th Congress of the Philippines|6th Congress]] until the end of the [[7th Congress of the Philippines|7th Congress]]. Davao del Sur was represented in the [[Interim Batasang Pambansa]] as part of [[Interim Batasang Pambansa#Regional Representatives|Region XI]] from 1978 to 1984, and returned [[#At-Large (defunct)|two representatives, elected at-large]], to the [[Regular Batasang Pambansa]] in [[1984 Philippine parliamentary election|1984]]. [[Davao City]] separately elected its [[Legislative districts of Davao City#At-Large (defunct)|own representatives]] starting that year. Under the new Constitution which was proclaimed on February 11, 1987, Davao del Sur was reapportioned into two congressional districts;{{cite web|title=1987 Constitution of the Philippines - Apportionment Ordinance|website=Official Gazette of the Republic of the Philippines|url=http://www.officialgazette.gov.ph/constitutions/the-1987-constitution-of-the-republic-of-the-philippines/the-1987-constitution-of-the-republic-of-the-philippines-ordinance/|author=1986 Constitutional Commission|date=February 2, 1987|access-date=November 19, 2017}} each elected its member to the restored [[House of Representatives of the Philippines|House of Representatives]] starting [[1987 Philippine legislative election|that same year]]. The passage of Republic Act No. 10360{{cite web|title=Republic Act No. 10360 - An Act Creating the Province of Davao Occidental|url=http://www.officialgazette.gov.ph/2013/01/14/republic-act-no-10360/|website=Official Gazette of the Republic of the Philippines|author=Congress of the Philippines|access-date=February 3, 2017|location=Metro Manila, Philippines|date=January 14, 2013}} and its subsequent [[2013 Davao Occidental creation plebiscite|ratification by plebiscite]] in 2013 separated five southern municipalities of [[Davao del Sur]] to create the province of [[Davao Occidental]]. Per Section 7 of R.A. 10360, Davao del Sur's own representation was reduced to a single congressional district. The newly reconfigured [[#Lone District|lone district]] elected its representative in the [[2016 Philippine House of Representatives elections|2016 elections]]. == Lone District == *'''Population (2015)''': 632,588{{cite web|url=https://psa.gov.ph/sites/default/files/attachments/hsd/pressrelease/2015_Table%201_Legislative%20Districts.xlsx|website=Philippine Statistics Authority|date=2015|title=Population of Population of Legislative Districts by Region, Province, and Selected Highly Urbanized/Component City: 2015|access-date=November 19, 2017}} {| class="wikitable" style="text-align:center; width:40%;" |- ! width="40%"| Period !
